newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister preparing Kurd rebel amnesty law.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister preparing Kurd rebel amnesty law.

text.p: A Turkish cabinet member said on Friday he was preparing a law for a partial amnesty of thousands of Kurdish prisoners convicted of links to separatist rebels.

"The aim of preparing the draft law is to give an amnesty to prisoners who had been forced into aiding and abetting the terrorist organisation," State Minister Salim Ensarioglu told Reuters. The amnesty would have to be passed by parliament.

Ensarioglu said he had received backing on Thursday from Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, the head of his True Path Party, for his bid to free people convicted of helping the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebel group.

Aiding and abetting the PKK is a catch-all charge often used to jail those suspected of Kurdish nationalist sympathies. Ensarioglu, himself a Kurd, said official figures showed there were between 5,000 and 6,000 people in jail for aiding the PKK.
But he said the real figure was nearer 10,000 people.
More than 21,000 people have died in 12 years of conflict between the security forces and the guerrillas, fighting for Kurdish self-rule in the southeast of the country.

"The law will provide peace and harmony," Ensarioglu said. Previous attempts to declare an amnesty for the rebels or their backers have failed under pressure from the military and rightwingers in parliament.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan last year ruled out direct talks with the PKK, regarded by Turkey as a terrorist group.
